newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China province's foreign trade up 6.7 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China province's foreign trade up 6.7 pct in 1996.

text.p: Foreign trade in China's Guangdong province grew 6.7 percent year-on-year to $100.17 billion in 1996, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.
Exports rose 6.2 percent to $59.1 billion last year and imports climbed 7.6 percent to $41.07 billion, the newspaper said.
Overseas-funded enterprises were the major exporters, handling exports totalling $30.327 billion, up 22.8 percent over 1995, it said.
Foreign investment in the province totalled $13.9 billion in 1996, up 14 percent over the previous year, the newspaper said.
But it said contracted overseas investment declined 33 percent to $17.45 billion. No explanation was given for the fall.
The Guangdong government expects exports to rise eight percent year-on-year to $65 billion in 1997 and actual foreign investment to roughly equal the 1996 level, the newspaper said.

Last week, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said overseas investment in Guangdong's boomtown of Shenzhen rose 39.59 percent year-on-year to a record $2.422 billion in 1996, with the city's neighbour Hong Kong remaining the biggest investor.
